new_statements.quote: Il nous a paru adéquat d'attribuer un accent structurel à tous les thèmes et radicaux de la langue. Cet accent se place de la manière suivante : 1) Sur la seconde syllabe d'un thème trisyllabique à condition que la syllabe finale soit de type NCV. exemple : /-bàdùngù "canard" 2) Dans tous les autres cas, sur la syllabe qui suit immédiatement la limite du thème ou celle du radical. [...] L'accent est régulièrement présent sur la syllabe initiale des thèmes nominaux et des radicaux verbaux. Il en est de même pour les thèmes pronominaux. Toutefois, le connectif ne porte jamais aucun accent [...] aucun mot monosyllabique n'est jamais accentué en gisira.
new_statements.translation: We found it appropriate to assign a structural accent to all themes (stems) and radicals (roots) of the language. This accent is placed as follows: 1) on the second syllable of a trisyllabic stem provided the final syllable is of NCV type, e.g. /-bàdùngù/ 'duck'; 2) in all other cases, on the syllable immediately following the stem boundary or the root boundary. [...] The accent is regularly present on the initial syllable of nominal stems and verbal roots. The same holds for pronominal stems. However, the connective never bears any accent [...] no monosyllabic word is ever accented in Gisira.
new_statements.citation: Dodo-Bounguendza, Eric. 1993. Esquisse phonologique et morphologique du gisira, langue bantoue (B 41) du Gabon. Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles. Vol. 1.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gisira is a two-tone (H/L) language that additionally has a non-contrastive demarcative accent, realised phonetically as vowel lengthening (p. 52: 'Tout phonème vocalique situé dans une syllabe accentuée est représenté par son allophone long'). The structural accent falls on the stem-initial (root-initial) syllable of nouns, verbs and pronominals; CVCVNCV noun stems instead carry it on their second (penultimate) syllable. Word-final syllables never bear accent: a monosyllabic stem in word-final position throws its accent back onto the preceding prefix (rule 19.1), and an accent left before a word/phrase boundary is deleted (rule 24). Monosyllabic words (e.g. the connective) are never accented.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Rules 19.2, 21.1, 21.2 (pp. 156-158): a VNC syllable before final -V, and any non-final syllable separated by one syllable from an accented syllable, acquire a secondary accent (words of >=5 syllables, or 4 with initial accent); rule 26.2 deletes the first of two adjacent accents.
new_statements.exceptions: CVCVNCV noun themes accented on penult rather than stem-initial (/gibadungù/ 'canard' vs /gipukùlù/ 'chapeau', p. 157); plural postfinal -anu carries its own accent (p. 154); apocopated verbs join the accent group of the following object (p. 161); author calls the analysis provisional ('ni exhaustif ni définitif', p. 153) and tempo-dependent.
new_statements.domain_note: Accent = vowel length, demarcative; in slow speech every non-monosyllabic word has at least one accent, at faster tempo only the word before a pause/phrase boundary keeps it (pp. 162-163), so surface length marks the word in citation/slow forms but the phrase-final word in connected speech. Lexical tone (H/B) is independent and contrastive. Variety: speakers from Ngounié province (Fougamou/Mandji area Gisira).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Gisira (isira, B41) as spoken by three informants from Ngounié province, Gabon (the Fougamou/Mandji Gisira that Blanchon calls 'eshira de Fougamou, gisir gi kamba'); this is the language-level variety sira1266 itself, not a divergent dialect. Mouguiama 1993 (not seen) treats a distinct dialect, Ngosi.
